## Control `peer`

The peer app's boot (routed at /peer/): the constellation — the peer feed and force layout driving the scene facet through the player brick — plus the add-connection and update dialogs. COMMAND HOST: peers, info, local, remote, discovery.

### peer.peer.info

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Reports this instance's system and network information as a JSONObject: local IP addresses, machine and application identifiers, and service ports. Takes the String `nn_sessionid` supplied by the frame, plus `uuid` (Any) and `salt` (Any) — when `uuid` carries a list of peer ids their connection details are resolved and included, obscured using `salt`. Nulls for both give local information only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | The unique session ID assigned to this request |
| `uuid` | Any | no | A list of peer IDs to retrieve details about. Pass null for none — the param is still required (newbound commands have no optional parameters). |
| `salt` | Any | no | The cryptographic salt used together with `uuid` when resolving peer details. Pass null when `uuid` is null — the param is still required. |

**HTTP:** `GET /peer/info`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies \
  "http://localhost:8080/peer/info"
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"peer","cmd":"info","params":{}}
```

**MCP tool:** `peer-peer-info`

**See also:** [discovery](#peerpeerdiscovery), [local](#peerpeerlocal), [peers](#peerpeerpeers), [remote](#peerpeerremote)

### peer.peer.local

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Execute the given remote request as a local HTTP request.

*(inferred)* Runs `request` through this instance's own HTTP handling under the caller's session. A 404 comes back as an error result. When the answer is a file or a byte stream, the content is sent to the calling peer over a new peer stream, and the result carries that `stream_id` instead of the body.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | JSONObject | yes | The `JSONObject` representing the client's request, containing parameters for the local operation. It is used to prepare and execute a data retrieval, potentially leading to a file download or stream. |
| `nn_session` | JSONObject | server | This request metadata is provided by the Newbound framework automatically. |
| `nn_sessionid` | String | server | This request metadata is provided by the Newbound framework automatically. |

**HTTP:** `GET /peer/local`

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/peer/local" \
  --data-urlencode 'request={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"peer","cmd":"local","params":{"request":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `peer-peer-local`

**See also:** [discovery](#peerpeerdiscovery), [info](#peerpeerinfo), [peers](#peerpeerpeers), [remote](#peerpeerremote)

### peer.reboot.reboot

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `FLAT` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

"Reboot the computer" — honestly, on every OS. Picks an ordered plan by std::env::consts::OS (linux: systemctl reboot, then loginctl reboot, then sudo -n reboot; macos: osascript System Events restart, then sudo -n shutdown -r now; windows: shutdown /r /t 0; anything else is unsupported), resolves each tool on PATH (Windows also tries PATHEXT extensions; a missing tool counts as a failed attempt "not installed"), and runs each attempt with a 10 s timeout, keeping exit code and stderr. FLAT replies: success {status:ok, method}; failure {status:err, msg, attempts:[{cmd,code,err}]} with msg naming the machine and the per-OS fix (polkit/sudoers on Linux, Automation permission or sudoers on macOS, the shut-down right on Windows). When config.properties has reboot_dryrun=true it runs nothing and answers {status:ok, dryrun:true, plan, os}. The pure helpers reboot_plan(os) and failure_message(os, machine, attempts) (plus find_on_path/run_attempt/machine_name) are pub at module level so every OS's plan and wording can be checked without running anything.

No parameters.

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=peer&id=sqgqnm18434391301x302&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=peer' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=sqgqnm18434391301x302' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"peer","id":"sqgqnm18434391301x302","args":{}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `peer-reboot-reboot`

**See also:** [init](#peerrebootinit)

## Control `service`

COMMAND HOST for the P2P transport service: listen (tcp/udp), connect, streams, the remote-exec relay, maintenance. Runs the peer network; not a UI.

### peer.service.close_stream

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `JSONObject` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

This command closes a specified live stream, identified by `uuid` and `streamid`, for a given user. Depending on the `write` parameter, it terminates either the read or write end of the stream and returns an empty JSON object.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uuid` | String | yes | The UUID of the peer this stream is with |
| `streamid` | Integer | yes | The ID of the stream to close |
| `write` | Boolean | yes | Indicates whether the stream is for reading or writing. |

**HTTP:** `GET /app/exec?lib=peer&id=vmxtup18d3d4e87benff&args=…` (via `app.app.exec`)

```bash
curl -b nb.cookies -G \
  "http://localhost:8080/app/exec" \
  --data-urlencode 'lib=peer' \
  --data-urlencode 'id=vmxtup18d3d4e87benff' \
  --data-urlencode 'args={"uuid":"<uuid>","streamid":0,"write":false}'
```

**WebSocket frame:**

```text
cmd {"pid":"1","bot":"app","cmd":"exec","params":{"lib":"peer","id":"vmxtup18d3d4e87benff","args":{"uuid":"<uuid>","streamid":0,"write":false}}}
```

**MCP tool:** `peer-service-close_stream`

**See also:** [get_stream](#peerserviceget_stream), [new_stream](#peerservicenew_stream), [stream_write](#peerservicestream_write)

### peer.service.get_stream

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `InputStream` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Retrieves an `InputStream` by first locating the peer identified by `uuid` and establishing the best available connection, then joining the specified `stream_id` on that connection. The command incorporates a retry mechanism to ensure successful stream retrieval.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uuid` | String | yes | The UUID of the remote peer |
| `stream_id` | Integer | yes | The ID of the existing stream to join |


### peer.service.listen

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `Integer` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

### peer.service.new_stream

**Language:** rust · **Returns:** `Integer` · **Groups:** (not set) · **Readers:** `[]`

Creates a new communication stream for the peer identified by the provided unique UUID. It attempts to establish the stream on the peer's best available connection, returning an integer stream ID on success, or -1 if the peer or a suitable connection cannot be found.
